dedupe_keys.name: gnss sdr open source software defined gnss receiver

description: GNSS-SDR is an open-source software-defined receiver for global navigation satellite systems, developed since 2011 under the lead of Carles Fernández-Prades at the Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya near Barcelona. Written in C++ on top of the GNU Radio framework, it performs the whole receiver chain in software: detection, synchronisation, demodulation and decoding of the navigation message, computation of observables and position fixes. It processes GPS L1 C/A, L2C and L5, Galileo E1b/c, E5a, E5b and E6B, GLONASS L1 and L2 C/A, BeiDou B1I and B3I, and QZSS L1 C/A and L5 signals, from a wide range of radio front-ends or raw sample files, and writes standard outputs such as RINEX and RTCM. It also offers monitoring of the receiver's internal state and a testing framework for key performance indicators, and a custom Linux distribution, Geniux, runs it on embedded devices. The current release is v0.0.21, published on 14 April 2026. Coverage: software, any location. Format and access: C++ source on GitHub and packages for Linux distributions, free under GPL v3 or later. Caveats: needs signal-processing knowledge and suitable radio front-ends for live use; performance depends on the host computer. Simulation uses: testing receiver resilience to interference and spoofing with recorded or simulated signals, and building hardware-in-the-loop digital twins of positioning chains. Related records: FGI-GSRx is a MATLAB receiver, GNU Radio is the underlying framework, and the FGI and Fraunhofer interference datasets provide test signals.
